annotations.text: EVERY FIGURE IS THE ENGINE'S. The search is q_056 "gym leggings with pockets", 43bp of WEEKLY_VOLUME 430,000 = 1,849 a week. The ladder is one real resolveAuction() on that search at 19:00, seed 20260902, with the rival ads from content/adCopy.js: Marlow 1st paying Rs 25.13 on a Rs 30 bid, Halcyon 2nd paying Rs 9.45 on Rs 16 with a better-fitting ad. Six of nine entered; three had no keyword that matched. Order value Rs 2,400 and margin 52% are setup.js's briefing() for mid. Freight Rs 200 is RTO_FREIGHT_PAISE, charged on a parcel refused at the door. Roughly four orders in ten come back (mid, 41.7%).

WORD BUDGET, MEASURED PER SCREEN. Corrected 2026-09-19 while building the words: this annotation first said 167 words, which counted the prose and not the labels, kickers, columns and buttons. Over every line the run is 477 - 297 prose, 139 label, 41 instruction - against round 0's 781 over five steps. But a total was never the figure that matters: a beginner drowns on a SCREEN. Round 0's step 1 is 281 words, about 248 visible at once, and that is the step a stranger gave up inside. The bound is no beat over 80 words on screen. Today beat 1 is 75 carrying the opening statement, beat 3 is 65, nothing else reaches 62. Nothing here repeats a guide chapter: the run teaches the world (search, ad, position, impression, auction, bid, ad rank, click, cost per click, budget, conversion, the delay, return), and the ground-floor chapters teach the controls (keyword, match type, positioning, landing page). One word, one home.

ONE BEAT AT A TIME, advanced by the player. No autoplay and no timers - a timer would freeze in the browser pane and record nothing (HANDOVER's known traps). Played beats collapse to one quiet line and stay on screen, so nothing is lost and a re-reader can scroll back. Skip is on every board but the last. The last board offers 'Watch that again', which is also how the Guide reopens it. Beat 5 was one board with beat 6 until the owner split them on 2026-09-19: the delay and the return are the two hardest ideas in the run and they were sharing the board where attention is thinnest.

MOTION IS THE REVIEW'S OWN (slc-review section 13), not invented here. Transform and opacity only, no library. A beat enters on opacity 0 to 1 and translateY 8px to 0, 240ms, cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) - section 13 row 2. Moving between beats is direction-aware, 260ms, cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1) - row 3. The ladder reveals row by row at a 50ms stagger and its bars grow from zero, which is row 5's end-screen reveal applied to the same idea, nine brands in rank order. NO COUNTING TICKERS anywhere: every rupee figure appears at its true value, because a ticker shows numbers the engine never reported. Under prefers-reduced-motion every translate is dropped and the fades stay. Four motions in all, inside section 13's cap of five to seven for the whole app.
